subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: Should #87051 remain open until maintainers have live current-main proof for spawned-subagent Codex OAuth, or is source-level main-agent OAuth read-through enough to close it?
rationale: The current source direction looks right, but the reported failure is a production auth/provider fallback path where a missed agentDir handoff can silently route work to another provider.

options.title: Keep Open For Live Proof
options.body: Require a live current-main sessions_spawn run showing the child agent uses the inherited Codex/OpenAI OAuth profile before closing.

options.title: Close After Source Review
options.body: Close now based on main-agent OAuth read-through and Codex owner-resolution source/tests, accepting that live spawned-subagent proof is still absent.

options.title: Split Diagnostics Follow-Up
options.body: Close auth propagation only after proof, then track any remaining fallback-warning or fail-closed policy as a narrower issue.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Live Proof
recommendation.body: Require a live current-main sessions_spawn run showing the child agent uses the inherited Codex/OpenAI OAuth profile before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history links steipete to OpenAI provider identity, Codex auth bridge, and session ownership decisions across the affected boundary.
